questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: It is a unique opportunity, to try something different and experience a new place.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I found my destination intriguing and I had not been there and wanted to explore it.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great experience with study abroad, but there are always opticals when doing something different that you haven't tried before.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy enough, but there was a lot of information that you need and that was be a little overwhelming.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international office was a big help and other exchanges students was also a big help.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: again the assistance and orientation was good, but because everything was new it was still a little overwhelming.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Student housing could be applied for, where there was different options depending on your needs and it was relatively easy.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My room included a common kitchen, that I shared with the other people living on my floor.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is a great way to meet people and it ensures that you don´t get scammed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was expencive, but i think it would have been difficult to find anything cheaper on my own

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had some trouble with registering for courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to register for courses before arrival and then when we arrived we had about 20 days to change it, if you wanted to take other courses or some of the chosen courses had changes timetable or was chancelled.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office was helpful, but they had a lot of people they needed to help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It took me a long time to finally register for the classes that I wanted, but it worked out in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: they are very chill about the regstration because you can changes it for some time after arrival, so eventhough it is a little stressfull it will all work out, they are helpfull!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I felt they didn't have a lot that fit my academic profile.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was fitting, but there were a lot of assignments that need to be handed in or presented to pass the courses and this was a little stressful because there were a lot of submission dates that you needed to keep track of.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The many assignments required for passing were very different. It was good in a way that you had to engage more in the courses, and the final exam didn't make your hole grade, but it was also a lot of work during the semester, where at UCPH you are more in charge of you time and effort.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a very cheap gym at the university.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I dont know, I mostly did activities non related to the university.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The pool is very nice and so is the events a the student cellar.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is so much stuff to see in Iceland and many opportunities for weekend trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy enough I would say, but I mostly spend time with other exchange students so maybe I didn't adjust that much.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I wouldn't know.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing comes to mind.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their very laid-back attitude to life.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Rent a car and go on trips. 
You will see northern lights don't stress about it. 
Have fun and enjoy your stay it is a one in a live time experience.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is okay to not have everything figured out before coming, you will figure it out as you go.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the wonderful friends I made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The seasonal change in light hours.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
